# Documentation Index

`docs/ja/` is the authoritative Japanese source for public documentation. The English and Korean versions are generated by the R22 translation pipeline; do not edit `docs/en/` or `docs/ko/` directly. `docs/ja/reference/` is also generated from code by R21, so do not edit it directly.

## Reading Order

- **First-time users**: [Feature Overview](overview.md) → [Overall Architecture](architecture/index.md) → [Memory System](memory/index.md). For the flow of operation, read [Lifecycle](architecture/lifecycle.md).
- **Those interested in design**: [Design Philosophy](vision.md) → [Correspondence with Neuroscience](brain-mapping.md) → [Overall Architecture](architecture/index.md) → the memory chapters.
- **Operators**: [Configuration](operations/configuration.md) → [Security](security.md) → [CLI Reference](reference/cli.md) and [Configuration Reference](reference/config.md). For individual integrations, refer to [Slack](integrations/slack.md), [Zoom](integrations/zoom.md), and [AnimaWorks Hub](integrations/hub.md).

## For Writers

- Use the "である" style. Place `> 確認したコミット: <短縮 sha>` at the top of each file to indicate the code revision against which the content was verified.
- For code references, write the path and symbol name as in `core/memory/priming/engine.py`'s `_prime_compact`. Do not include line numbers.
- Enclose identifiers, configuration keys, paths, and commands in backticks so they can be protected during translation.
- Do not create a list of configuration keys in the body; link to the [Configuration Reference](reference/config.md) instead. In the body, only mention keys needed to explain behavior.
- Do not describe deprecated features or past implementation history. Change history is the role of the CHANGELOG.
- Headings serve as translation diff units. Keep each section to roughly 2,000 characters or less.
- As a rule, record each fact in one place, and link to detailed chapters from overviews and correspondence tables.
